title: Developer Experience Lighthouse: initiative-level OKR tracker for SDKs & Quickstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable initiative-level tracking and playbook (the "DevX Lighthouse") to coordinate SDKs, docs, and quickstarts initiatives across cycles. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-success for new customers by 30% and increase SDK adoption by 20% in H1 2026 through cohort-based onboarding, standardized telemetry, and a lightweight OKR cadence for PM/Eng/Design.

Scope: 1) Define initiative OKR template and success metrics (A1: TtFS, A2: SDK activation, A3: retention at 14d). 2) Build a single dashboard + dataset that surfaces cohort funnels (signup -> sample app run -> first API call -> production pin). 3) Run 3 quickstart cohort experiments (JS SDK, Python SDK, Self-hosted Private deploy) with A/B variations on sample apps and docs. 4) Publish the Lighthouse playbook (Confluence) and a public checklist for Solutions/SEs.

Deliverables: Lighthouse OKR template, shared dashboard (Console), 3 cohort runs with experiment summaries, playbook doc + rollup PRD, and a set of SDK/quickstart changes tied to measured regressions/improvements.

Success metrics (targets): "time_to_first_success": "-30% vs baseline Q4 2025", "sdk_activation_rate": "+20%", "quickstart_dropoff_1st_hour": "-25%". Primary metric owner: Growth/DevX partnership; Product owner: PM (assignee).

Risks & trade-offs: 1) Instrumentation surface — richer telemetry improves signal but increases storage and privacy review overhead. 2) Resource load — cohort experiments require engineering time for sample apps and runbook automation. 3) Too many simultaneous experiments could pollute signals; we will gate to 3 live cohorts per cycle.

Stakeholders & approvals: DevX PM, SDK eng leads (Python/JS), Docs lead (Marta Liu), Solutions Eng, Privacy/Legal (for telemetry scope).

Notes on scope decisions: scoped out mass localization for initial cohorts; prioritized canonical English quickstarts and one sample app per language.
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with SDK leads (JS: @Diego Ramos, Python: @Priya Shah) and Docs (Marta Liu). Agreed on 3 initial cohorts and gating criteria. Action: engineers to estimate sample app work by 2026-03-10.

2026-03-05: Telemetry design draft posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/devx/lighthouse/telemetry-design. Feedback from Privacy: limit IP/geo capture; use hashed identifiers. Security review flagged retention policy; added to dependencies.

2026-03-08: Engineering estimates in. Total ~3.5 sprint-equivalents across teams. Prioritization call decided to run JS SDK cohort first (fastest path) and schedule Python in next cycle. Added label 'cohort-experiments'.

2026-03-09: Dashboard prototype available: https://app.redwood.ai/console/dashboards/devx-lighthouse. Early funnel shows baseline TtFS=18m for internal beta. Action: create instrumentation PRs and a test harness for cohort runs.

2026-03-11: PR for JS quickstart changes opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devx/pull/4123. Requested review from Docs and SDK lead. Noted a UX trade-off: single-file sample app reduces friction but hides config complexity for private deployments; decided to provide both 'quickstart' and 'advanced' lanes.

2026-03-12: Canary cohort cohort-01 (JS SDK) scheduled to start on 2026-03-16 for a 2-week run. Created experiment hypothesis doc and accepted it in the playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/devx/lighthouse/experiments/canary-01.
